caption_judgement: all four captions are substantive rather than restatements of the panel titles: they name the machine and shot, the shared level array, the grey/blue series mapping, the residual and convergence values, and the mechanical text-bound check, so no caption finding is recorded.

figures.identification: The attachment order is not recorded, so each PNG was identified from its rendered content. image-0 draws a vessel unlike the one shared by image-1 and image-3 (scale-normalised wall overlap IoU 0.08), a single closed D-contour with divertor legs below the chamber, which is the wall tests/test_equilibrium_forward_reference.py takes for the ITER reference case from the equilibrium limiter unit[0].outline; it is the remaining generating/recovered pair, so it is iter.svg: the only other generating/recovered figure the run commits.

image-1 draws the same vessel outline as image-3 (scale-normalised overlap of the two wall tracings gives IoU 0.81, against 0.08 for image-0's wall), and the committed mast-generating-refusal.svg is drawn by the run's render_failure.py from _physical_problem('mast'), whose wall is profile.operator.wall.coordinate; the shared vessel is therefore the MAST 22086/43 first wall and image-1 is the MAST generating/recovered pair.
image-2 is the analytic Solov'ev panel pair: an elliptic first wall with concentric closed contours and a single axis marker in each panel and no X-point, exactly the state the caption describes.

image-3 is the only attachment carrying the 'stored starting field' / 'rejected terminal field' titles and the legend 'starting field and its nulls' / 'terminal field; no admitted axis', and it draws the MAST vessel shared with mast.svg.

findings.summary: In each generating/recovered pair (image-0 iter.svg, image-1 mast.svg, image-2 solovev.svg) the loop draws the generating null markers first and the recovered markers second at the same coordinates, with the recovered style at the default size on top, so the rendered left-hand panel shows the recovered (blue) marker as its dominant null with the grey generating marker surviving only as a thin rim (measured as a single-pixel grey outline around the blue triangle in image-0 and image-1). The legend assigns blue to the recovered series, so a reader looking at the generating panel alone sees a recovered-coloured null on the generating state; the caption explains that both sets are drawn and coincide, and nothing is misread as data, but the 'both null sets' encoding is much weaker than the caption claims and the rim may vanish where the page serves the 1400 px canvas into a narrower column.

The right-hand panel draws the starting field's grey axis triangle and X marker inside the rejected terminal field's blue contour ring, and the blue terminal field carries no marker of its own by design. A reader who skims the panel sees a grey axis marker sitting in the terminal field's ring and can take it for the terminal field's axis, which is exactly the panel's subject; the caption does say the grey markers in both panels belong to the starting field, but the image alone does not distinguish those two readings.
